source_row.stem: Buprenorphine, like methadone, may be used during pregnancy for opioid use disorder because:
source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Considered contraindicated in every pregnant client without exception, despite being a recognized medication-assisted treatment option","B":"It is a recognized medication-assisted treatment option, associated with less severe neonatal abstinence syndrome in some studies compared to methadone","C":"Guaranteeing that absolutely no neonatal effects will occur whatsoever, rather than reducing the severity of effects seen with some alternative treatments","D":"Having no established clinical role during pregnancy for treating opioid use disorder at all"}}
source_row.rationale: Buprenorphine is a recognized medication-assisted treatment option during pregnancy, with some studies suggesting less severe neonatal abstinence syndrome compared to methadone, though newborn monitoring is still needed.
source_row.source_detail: Buprenorphine as a Pregnancy Treatment Option
